metais check — Check a package without data, and report every finding of every
step at once, or only the refusal of a package that cannot be read.

Usage:
  metais check [<package>] [--limit <name>=<value>]... [--json]

Examples:
  metais check
      Checks the source directory in the working directory.
  metais check report-1.0.0.metais
      Checks a packed package.
  metais check --json
      Prints every finding as one metais.check/1 document.

The package is a source directory, the current directory when omitted, or a
packed package file. check reads nothing but the package and writes nothing. It
runs every step in order: the source tree, the entries, the limits of the
package pack would write, the manifest and its guide's links, every schema with
its defaults, examples, consts, enums and required names, every template, the
cross-reference of templates against schemas, Office Open XML text runs, the
examples' layout, and the compiled form. Each step runs whatever an earlier one
found; a step whose input could not be made is named in one report.step_skipped
finding.

A package that cannot be read at all — its container, its entry names, its
digests or its source tree — is refused with the findings every command gives
it.

check exits 1 when any finding is an error; warnings do not fail it unless
--fail-on warning is given.

Operands:
  <package>
      A source directory, or a packed package file; the current directory when
      omitted. - is refused, since a package is read with random access.

Flags:
  --limit <name>=<value>
      Lower one resource limit for this run, to a whole number no higher than
      its default (a size may end in KiB, MiB or GiB). metais limits lists them.
      May be given more than once.
  --fail-on <severity>
      With warning, a warning fails the command with exit status 1 as an error
      does; no finding's severity changes. Values: error, warning. Default:
      error.
  --json
      Print the result as one JSON document on standard output.
  --color <when>
      Colour human output: auto colours a stream that is a terminal when
      NO_COLOR is unset or empty; always and never override NO_COLOR. Values:
      auto, always, never. Default: auto.
  -h, --help
      Print help to standard output and exit 0; nothing else runs.

Prints:
  Every finding, then a line counting the errors, warnings and notes, then the
  Next: block. With --json, one metais.check/1 document.

Refusals:
  limit.invalid
      A --limit names no limit, gives a malformed value, or tries to raise one.
      Next: metais check --help
  limit.package
      The package breaches one of its limits.
      Next: metais check <package>
  usage.bad_value
      A flag's value is missing, or is not one the flag accepts, or a flag that
      takes no value is given one.
      Next: metais check --help
  usage.package_from_stdin
      The package operand is -, standard input.
      Next: metais check --help
  usage.repeated_flag
      A flag that may be given once is given again.
      Next: metais check --help
  usage.unexpected_operand
      An operand the command does not take.
      Next: metais check --help
  usage.unknown_flag
      An argument that is not a flag the command accepts, an abbreviated flag,
      or one-letter aliases written together.
      Next: metais check --help

  Each line below is a family of codes: how many there are, the cause they share
  and their next step. 'metais help refusals check' lists every code, and help
  --json gives each code's own cause.

  example.layout (1)        An example's layout (layout), an error.
                            Next: metais check <package>
  manifest.* (44)           The manifest breaks one of its rules.
                            Next: metais check <package>
  manifest.guide_link_missing (1)
                            The manifest (guide link missing), a warning.
                            Next: metais check <package>
  manifest.input.* (2)      The manifest, an error. Next: metais check <package>
  output.container.* (3)    A container's profile, an error.
                            Next: metais check <package>
  output.container.space (1)
                            A container's profile (container: space), a warning.
                            Next: metais check <package>
  output.declaration.validate_kind (1)
                            An output's declaration (declaration: validate
                            kind), an error. Next: metais check <package>
  output.path.* (8)         An output's literal path, an error.
                            Next: metais check <package>
  package.* (47)            The package is refused. Next: metais check <package>
  package.layout.* (2)      The package's tree, a warning.
                            Next: metais check <package>
  report.step_skipped (1)   The report (step skipped), an info.
                            Next: metais check <package>
  schema.* (10)             An input schema is refused.
                            Next: metais check <package>
  schema.* (3)              A schema, an error. Next: metais check <package>
  schema.* (2)              A schema, a warning. Next: metais check <package>
  template.* (11)           An output's path, when or for_each does not parse.
                            Next: metais check <package>
  template.* (6)            A template or a manifest expression, a warning.
                            Next: metais check <package>
  template.* (8)            A template does not parse, an error.
                            Next: metais check <package>
  template.* (11)           A template or a manifest expression, an error.
                            Next: metais check <package>
